title: Microbatch contour slicer: length-aware micro-batching and kernel routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a length-aware 'contour slicer' microbatching stage that dynamically groups in-flight requests into compact clusters to minimize padding while exposing kernel-affinity hints to the runtime kernel selector. The feature targets mixed-sequence workloads (short prompts + long completions) where fixed bucketing wastes tokens and hurts throughput/cost.

Background: Existing bucketing strategies we have assume coarse fixed bins; they reduce variance but introduce significant padding overhead for skewed distributions. Prior work reduced padding via aggressive trimming and prefill prioritization, but we need a more adaptive runtime component that can: 1) cluster requests by effective remaining-seqlen profile, 2) split/merge clusters at runtime based on kernel efficiency signals, and 3) provide kernel-affinity hints (fast-attention vs memory-saver vs sparse-friendly) and scheduling priority for prefill vs decode phases.

Design overview: The Contour Slicer sits between the request ingress and the batcher. For each request it computes a lightweight length contour: {prefill_len_estimate, expected_decode_steps, token-footprint-estimate}. Contours are hashed into a 2D space and clustered using an online micro-kmeans with reservoir sampling and time decay. Clusters are labeled with bucket-widths and an 'evaporative padding budget' that allows short-lived small-clusters to merge into neighbors if waiting time exceeds threshold.

Kernel hints and routing: Each cluster produces a kernel-affinity score vector exposed to the kernel selector: {latency_score, memory_score, sparsity_score}. The kernel selector uses these scores along with current device occupancy to pick kernels and instance types (e.g., tensor-core-optimized or memory-optim). For decode scheduling the slicer will prioritize decode-heavy clusters with lower idle-wait thresholds to reduce p99 latency for interactive flows.

Prefill/Decode interplay: We distinguish prefill-heavy requests (large single-call contexts) and decode-heavy streams. The contour slicer tags requests and applies different merge heuristics: prefer coalescing prefill segments by seq-prefix similarity; for decode streams prefer small low-latency buckets and opportunistic coalescing only when within tail-safety window.

Trade-offs and heuristics: - Merge threshold vs latency: larger merges save padding but increase wait. We use a sliding window utility tradeoff (delta_cost_per_token vs added_latency_ms) to make local decisions. - Cluster churn: to avoid oscillation we damp cluster reassignments with exponential backoff. - Kernel hint fidelity: hints are soft; kernel selector may ignore them if instance constraints require it.

Acceptance criteria: - Reduce median padding tokens-per-request by at least 35% on a synthetic mixed workload (50% short prompts (<32 tokens) + 50% long prefill + decode flows). - No more than 5% regression in p99 tail latency for interactive (latency-sensitive) requests during 95th percentile traffic. - Throughput (tokens/sec) improves by at least 10% for end-to-end serving costs in our benchmark suite. - All features behind runtime feature-flag and canary rollout.

Testing & telemetry: - Unit tests for cluster lifecycle, merge/split heuristics, and kernel-hint serialization. - Integration test harness that replays recorded production traces to verify padding savings and latency impact. - Telemetry: new metrics: cluster_count, avg_padding_tokens, kernel_hint_match_rate, cluster_merge_rate, wait_time_distribution. Dashboards + alerts on padding regressions or p99 increases.

Rollout plan: 1) Internal alpha: run on 5% of traffic in a dedicated runtime pool with isolated GPU instances and verbose logging. 2) Canary: enable for a subset of customers with varied workloads (PLG apps + enterprise). 3) Gradual ramp tied to padding reduction and p99 guardrails.

Risks & mitigations: - Incorrect prefill_len_estimate can miscluster; mitigate with conservative initial estimates and online correction using actual prefill sizes. - Kernel selector mismatch causing suboptimal kernel choices: include fallback metrics and allow runtime to override slicer hints when throughput suffers. - Observability overhead: sample logs and aggregate counters; avoid per-request heavy logging in prod.

Artifacts and links: - Design doc: https://redwood.atl/confluence/contour-slicer-design-2026 - Telemetry dashboard (staging): https://telemetry.redwood/staging/dashboards/contour-slicer - Spike PR with micro-kmeans lib: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1876

Next steps: finish prototype (Diego) and land unit tests, create integration replay harness (SRE pairing), schedule alpha run for 2026-W11.
